data.description:
IntakeRetryResult.message reports 'had no intake record to clear, nothing to retrigger' whenever released is 0. That fires in two different situations, a ticket that was never admitted and a ticket whose dedup markers were already cleared. The operator cannot tell which, so it is unclear whether the retry did nothing because there was nothing to do or because a previous attempt already did it.

The message is also silent about the github.* side effect rows that clear_intake_dedup deliberately retains. Those rows are keyed by sha256 of task_id, execution_id, operation and target, so a retry, which always allocates a new execution id, cannot replay them. Retaining them is correct and they are the ledger of effects that already happened.

The silence invites the opposite conclusion. During the massgov pilot a retained github.commit row was assumed to be blocking the retry and was deleted by hand. Nothing in the output said the row was scoped to a spent execution and inert.

Split the two outcomes into distinct messages, and state what was retained and why it cannot block the retry.
data.title: ADEVX-121 Distinguish the two nothing-to-retrigger outcomes and report retained ledger rows
